title: cloud native OS Pulse project profile
description: One profile per project per edition. See schema/vocabularies.md for the meaning of every enumerated value.

text.description: Verbatim, from the project's own words.

method.description: How this version was determined, so the next edition repeats it identically.

tradeoffs.description: Required on every profile. A profile is not complete until both sides are filled in. This is the structural bias control: no project, including the one the authors maintain, gets to have only upsides.

maintainers_fact.description: The one concentration fact the data sheet shows (methodology section 9, rule 16): N of M maintainers work for a company, single vendor, or maintainer affiliation not published.

known_issues.description: Shown at the bottom of the data sheet (methodology section 9, rule 19). Only four kinds count: a documented defect, an install or update artifact that runs unchecked unless the adopter changes a setting, a stated stop of maintenance of a capability the matrix shows, and a checked gap between what the project states and what it delivers.

open_questions.description: Factual questions this edition could not settle from primary sources. Feeds maintainer-review.md.

configurablePaths.description: d02 only. Can the adopter change which paths are writable or persistent? Shown on the Mounts row of the data sheet (methodology section 9, rule 21's companion row). 'via-lifecycle-manager' is for a base distribution whose mount layout is set by the framework that manages it.

how.description: One line: what the adopter can change, and how.

viaBaseDistribution.description: d08 only. Architectures the entry's own components are built for, credited 'via your base distribution' (methodology section 9, rule 21). Only for an entry that builds the OS from a base distribution the adopter picks.

distributionOption.description: d07 only. One Kubernetes distribution an entry documents. A value with no source is not recorded.

detail.description: One short sentence: how it is offered, with its limits.

providerEntry.description: d08 only. One infrastructure provider and how far the entry gets there. level is the level the entry reaches on this provider. unknown reads 'Not documented' and needs no source. Every other level needs a source with a verbatim quote.

name.description: Only with provider 'other': the cloud's name.

tier.description: Who supports it, as the source says.

archs.description: Architectures the source names for this provider.

tool.description: A name from the entry's own d09 config_tools.

how.description: One line: how the entry gets there.

capabilityHow.description: Whether a capability is on without the adopter doing anything. always-on and default-on read 'On by default' on the data sheet, opt-in reads 'Optional' and marks the matrix cell Opt-in. platform-provided is kept for entries whose platform state is not recorded yet; a profile that knows the state uses always-on, default-on or opt-in with 'platform'.

bootTrustChain.description: d10 only. The Boot trust chain column. The capability rule: level is the highest level the entry can reach. When the adopter has to turn it on, how is opt-in, via names the mode or setting that reaches it, and default says where the default leaves you. Each of the three statements cites its own sources: how_sources, sources, default.sources. provided_by names the entry that provides the whole chain (Hadron, through Kairos).

platform.description: The platform feature that provides it, such as Trusted Launch.

limit.description: Where an on-by-default capability holds, when it does not hold everywhere.

via.description: The mode or setting that reaches the level, as the data sheet sentence names it.

via_tag.description: A shorter name for the matrix tag, where via is long.

via_detail.description: One short phrase that says what the mode is.

name.description: The default install or mode, with its article, as the subject of a sentence: 'the standard install'.

level.description: not-documented: no source says. not-established: a source says, but it covers only part of the entry or the evidence does not bear it out; reason says which.

reason.description: One short sourced clause that explains the level.

updateSignatureCheck.description: d04 only. The data sheet wording of the Update signature check column, under the same capability rule as bootTrustChain. The verdict stays in artifact_verification. checks is one clause that says what is checked. default.checks is off, not-required or not-documented.

limit.description: Where an on-by-default capability holds, when it does not hold everywhere.

addSoftware.description: d06 only. One way to add software to the OS itself. kind 'unknown' stands alone, with evidence UNKNOWN and 'searched'. Methodology rule 21: an entry that builds from a base distribution gets the base's package manager only if its own documentation says so.

how.description: One or two short sentences: how it is done, with its limits.

quote.description: Short verbatim excerpt supporting the claim.

version.description: Documentation version, where the source is versioned.

citation.description: A source copied from a dimension field, as recorded there.

normalized.description: Closed-vocabulary values, table-ready. Shape varies per dimension; see vocabularies.md. A data sheet row cites only the sources recorded for the fields it shows: <field>_sources next to the field, or the field's own sources when the field is a mapping. A dimension's sources list backs the dimension as a whole and is never cited for one row.

_sources$.description: The sources behind the normalized field of the same name without the _sources suffix. The data sheet row that shows that field cites them.

mounts_sources.description: d02 only. The sources behind the read-only, reset-on-reboot and persistent lines of the Mounts row.

distribution_options.description: d07 only. The Kubernetes distributions the entry documents, one entry per distribution from a closed vocabulary (schema/vocabularies.md), each with how it is offered and a source. Install tools such as kubeadm stay in 'distributions' as text. Read by the matrix filter 'Kubernetes distribution'.

providers.description: d08 only. Where the entry runs, one item per infrastructure provider from a closed list (schema/vocabularies.md), with how far it gets, who supports that, and which channel configures the node first. A provider with no source is recorded as unknown, with the places searched. Read by the matrix column 'Where it runs', its filters and the data sheet.

add_software.description: d06 only. How an adopter adds software to the OS itself (host-level software, not workloads). One entry per way, from a closed vocabulary (schema/vocabularies.md). Shown in the matrix column 'Adding software to the OS' and in the data sheet.

summary.description: One to three sentences. This is what appears in a comparison table. Never a bare yes/no.

inferred_from.description: Required when evidence is INFERRED. Names the evidence the inference rests on.

searched.description: Required when evidence is UNKNOWN. Says where we looked, so the next edition does not repeat the search blindly.

unknowns.description: Specific sub-questions inside this dimension that stayed unresolved, even when the dimension as a whole is DOCUMENTED.
